quests.word: As you all know, we've been using the old system for years, and it has served us well.
quests.textToSpeak: As you all know, we've been using the old system for years, and it has served us well.
options: Accelerating (familiar background is covered quickly because the audience already holds it)
Decelerating (shared history is given extra time to honour the old system)
quests.correctAnswer: Accelerating (familiar background is covered quickly because the audience already holds it)
quests.hint: Who in the room needs to be told this?
quests.explanation: Nobody. When information is shared, it works as a runway, and runways are covered quickly so the speaker can reach the new point.
quests.pacingRule: Accelerated Pacing: Old, shared information is delivered quickly.

quests.word: What's new is that the system will now log every change, and that applies to everyone.
quests.textToSpeak: What's new is that the system will now log every change, and that applies to everyone.
options: Accelerating (the speaker moves briskly because the change is technical)
Decelerating (the new rule and its reach are given the space that new information needs)
quests.correctAnswer: Decelerating (the new rule and its reach are given the space that new information needs)
quests.hint: Which part of this sentence would the audience have had no way of predicting?
quests.explanation: New information takes processing time, and 'applies to everyone' is what makes it personal. Slowing there helps people register that it affects them.
quests.pacingRule: Decelerated Pacing: New information is slower than old information.

quests.word: You know the old process, where you emailed three people? Forget it, there's a single form now.
quests.textToSpeak: You know the old process, where you emailed three people? Forget it, there's a single form now.
options: Decelerating (the question is light, and the replacement is delivered clearly)
Accelerating (the speaker stays brisk to sound relaxed about the change)
quests.correctAnswer: Decelerating (the question is light, and the replacement is delivered clearly)
quests.hint: After the light question, which words does the listener actually need to keep?
quests.explanation: The first sentence is the reference point that everyone shares. The second tells them what to do from now on.
quests.pacingRule: Decelerated Pacing: The replacement for a familiar routine is slowed.

quests.word: To give you some background, the project began two years ago, went through three managers, and was nearly cancelled twice.
quests.textToSpeak: To give you some background, the project began two years ago, went through three managers, and was nearly cancelled twice.
options: Accelerating (the history is a quick run-up to the main point)
Decelerating (the history is slow because it shows the project's struggle)
quests.correctAnswer: Accelerating (the history is a quick run-up to the main point)
quests.hint: What will the speaker say after this sentence, and will it matter more?
quests.explanation: Background supports the real message. Keeping it brisk signals to the audience that the main point is coming.
quests.pacingRule: Accelerated Pacing: Background is brisk.

quests.word: But here's the key point: none of that matters if we can't deliver by March.
quests.textToSpeak: But here's the key point: none of that matters if we can't deliver by March.
options: Decelerating (the main point is announced and then delivered deliberately)
Accelerating (the speaker speeds up to get to the deadline)
quests.correctAnswer: Decelerating (the main point is announced and then delivered deliberately)
quests.hint: Which phrase in the sentence tells you the speaker has reached the main point?
quests.explanation: 'Here's the key point' is a signal. The pace should match the signal, and slow down so that the audience knows it's the main point.
quests.pacingRule: Decelerated Pacing: Main points are slowed.

quests.word: Anyway, without going into all the history, let me get to the important bit.
quests.textToSpeak: Anyway, without going into all the history, let me get to the important bit.
options: Decelerating (the sentence is slowed to prepare the audience for the main point)
Accelerating (a verbal shortcut is delivered briskly, as it promises to skip)
quests.correctAnswer: Accelerating (a verbal shortcut is delivered briskly, as it promises to skip)
quests.hint: What is the sentence doing in the talk?
quests.explanation: It's a bridge. A bridge that drags defeats its purpose of skipping the history.
quests.pacingRule: Accelerated Pacing: Shortcuts in a talk are brisk.

quests.word: We'd been driving for about six hours, it was getting dark, and everyone was tired and hungry, when we saw the sign.
quests.textToSpeak: We'd been driving for about six hours, it was getting dark, and everyone was tired and hungry, when we saw the sign.
options: Accelerating (the scene-setting is brisk because it leads to the event)
Decelerating (the scene-setting is slowed to build suspense)
quests.correctAnswer: Accelerating (the scene-setting is brisk because it leads to the event)
quests.hint: What is this part of the story for?
quests.explanation: It's setting the scene. The important thing is what's next, and quick delivery shows that.
quests.pacingRule: Accelerated Pacing: Scene-setting is brisk.

quests.word: And the sign said, in big red letters, that the road ahead was closed.
quests.textToSpeak: And the sign said, in big red letters, that the road ahead was closed.
options: Accelerating (the narrator speeds up as the story accelerates)
Decelerating (the moment the story turns needs a slower beat)
quests.correctAnswer: Decelerating (the moment the story turns needs a slower beat)
quests.hint: Is this part of the set-up, or the moment the story turns?
quests.explanation: This is the point at which the plan falls apart. A measured pace lets the listener absorb it and gives the story weight.
quests.pacingRule: Decelerated Pacing: The turning point of a story is slowed.

quests.word: We ended up sleeping in the car, which was cold but honestly quite funny.
quests.textToSpeak: We ended up sleeping in the car, which was cold but honestly quite funny.
options: Accelerating (the wrap-up of the anecdote is light and rapid)
Decelerating (the ending is slowed to give it a serious tone)
quests.correctAnswer: Accelerating (the wrap-up of the anecdote is light and rapid)
quests.hint: What tone does the speaker want as the story finishes?
quests.explanation: The story ends on a light, humorous note, so the wrap-up is quick. A slow, solemn ending would suggest the night was a bigger problem than the speaker means.
quests.pacingRule: Accelerated Pacing: Light wrap-ups to stories are quick.

quests.word: Okay, that covers the first half, so let's shift gears and look at the numbers.
quests.textToSpeak: Okay, that covers the first half, so let's shift gears and look at the numbers.
options: Accelerating (a transition between sections is brisk)
Decelerating (the transition is slowed to give a clear division)
quests.correctAnswer: Accelerating (a transition between sections is brisk)
quests.hint: Does the audience need to remember this sentence?
quests.explanation: This is a signpost into the next section, and the audience just needs to follow it. A quick delivery keeps the talk moving; a slow one would stall the pace.
quests.pacingRule: Accelerated Pacing: A short signpost into the next section keeps the talk moving.

quests.word: Now, this next slide is the one I most want you to remember.
quests.textToSpeak: Now, this next slide is the one I most want you to remember.
options: Decelerating (the announcement of importance is delivered slowly)
Accelerating (the speaker speeds up to get to the slide)
quests.correctAnswer: Decelerating (the announcement of importance is delivered slowly)
quests.hint: What is the speaker asking the audience to do with their attention?
quests.explanation: The speaker is flagging a moment. The flag works only if the speaker slows down.
quests.pacingRule: Decelerated Pacing: Signals of importance are slowed.

quests.word: Right, so, moving on, unless anybody has a burning question about that.
quests.textToSpeak: Right, so, moving on, unless anybody has a burning question about that.
options: Accelerating (the transition is brisk and keeps the meeting moving)
Decelerating (the phrase is slowed to give time for questions)
quests.correctAnswer: Accelerating (the transition is brisk and keeps the meeting moving)
quests.hint: Is the speaker really inviting questions?
quests.explanation: 'Unless anybody has a burning question' is a polite formality, and the speed tells the audience there's no need to stop. A slow version would genuinely invite interruptions.
quests.pacingRule: Accelerated Pacing: Polite formalities in transitions are brisk.

quests.word: An escrow account is a neutral account where the money is held until both sides have met their obligations.
quests.textToSpeak: An escrow account is a neutral account where the money is held until both sides have met their obligations.
options: Accelerating (the definition is quick because the speaker has said it many times)
Decelerating (a new term is given processing time so the meaning can form)
quests.correctAnswer: Decelerating (a new term is given processing time so the meaning can form)
quests.hint: What is the listener's experience of the word 'escrow'?
quests.explanation: It's new. The listener must build a meaning as they hear it, and that takes time.
quests.pacingRule: Decelerated Pacing: New concepts are slowed.

quests.word: It's basically a spreadsheet, but online, so everyone can see it.
quests.textToSpeak: It's basically a spreadsheet, but online, so everyone can see it.
options: Decelerating (the comparison is slowed so the audience knows it's an analogy)
Accelerating (a familiar comparison is given lightly and quickly)
quests.correctAnswer: Accelerating (a familiar comparison is given lightly and quickly)
quests.hint: Is the speaker introducing a new idea or linking to a known one?
quests.explanation: Spreadsheets are familiar. The speaker uses the known thing to help the new thing, and doesn't need to linger.
quests.pacingRule: Accelerated Pacing: Familiar analogies are quick.

quests.word: The word 'fatigue' in engineering doesn't mean tiredness, it refers to weakening caused by repeated stress.
quests.textToSpeak: The word 'fatigue' in engineering doesn't mean tiredness, it refers to weakening caused by repeated stress.
options: Accelerating (the speaker speeds up to get past a point that seems obvious)
Decelerating (the contrast between the everyday and technical meaning is clear)
quests.correctAnswer: Decelerating (the contrast between the everyday and technical meaning is clear)
quests.hint: Which everyday meaning is the audience likely to assume?
quests.explanation: Everyone knows 'tired'. The real definition replaces a belief, so the swap has to be heard.
quests.pacingRule: Decelerated Pacing: Redefinitions of familiar words are slowed.

quests.word: If you take one thing away from today, let it be this: ask for help early.
quests.textToSpeak: If you take one thing away from today, let it be this: ask for help early.
options: Accelerating (the speaker speeds up to end on an energetic note)
Decelerating (the single takeaway is given a clear, unhurried delivery)
quests.correctAnswer: Decelerating (the single takeaway is given a clear, unhurried delivery)
quests.hint: What would the audience do if they could only remember one sentence?
quests.explanation: Listeners remember the sentence the speaker made space for. Slowing down on the one takeaway marks it as the one to keep; speeding up would bury it among the other lines.
quests.pacingRule: Decelerated Pacing: The sentence you want remembered is slowed.

quests.word: There are a few other things I could mention, but they're in the handout.
quests.textToSpeak: There are a few other things I could mention, but they're in the handout.
options: Accelerating (pointing to supplementary material is quick)
Decelerating (the speaker slows to draw attention to the handout)
quests.correctAnswer: Accelerating (pointing to supplementary material is quick)
quests.hint: How important are these 'other things' to the talk?
quests.explanation: The speaker is moving away from them. A brisk pace makes it clear that they're optional.
quests.pacingRule: Accelerated Pacing: Supplementary points are quick.

quests.word: The real issue, and I want to be clear about this, isn't the cost, it's the trust.
quests.textToSpeak: The real issue, and I want to be clear about this, isn't the cost, it's the trust.
options: Accelerating (the speaker speeds up through the parenthetical and the contrast)
Decelerating (the correction of the obvious cause is delivered slowly)
quests.correctAnswer: Decelerating (the correction of the obvious cause is delivered slowly)
quests.hint: What did the audience assume before this sentence?
quests.explanation: The audience assumed cost. The speaker has to shift that, so 'isn't the cost, it's the trust' needs time.
quests.pacingRule: Decelerated Pacing: The contrast that changes the audience's view is slowed.

quests.word: She opened the envelope, read it twice, and then quietly put it down.
quests.textToSpeak: She opened the envelope, read it twice, and then quietly put it down.
options: Accelerating (the narration speeds up to keep the story moving)
Decelerating (the quiet actions are narrated at a hushed, steady pace)
quests.correctAnswer: Decelerating (the quiet actions are narrated at a hushed, steady pace)
quests.hint: What is happening in the story at this point?
quests.explanation: The character is reacting to something significant, and the pace of the narration gives a sense of weight.
quests.pacingRule: Decelerated Pacing: Quiet moments in narration are slow.

quests.word: Then everything happened at once, the phones rang, the doors opened, and people started shouting.
quests.textToSpeak: Then everything happened at once, the phones rang, the doors opened, and people started shouting.
options: Accelerating (the chaotic sequence is narrated quickly to match)
Decelerating (the list is slowed so each event has equal weight)
quests.correctAnswer: Accelerating (the chaotic sequence is narrated quickly to match)
quests.hint: What does the sentence say about the pace of events?
quests.explanation: 'Everything at once' describes speed, so the telling copies it. A slow, even list would make the chaos sound orderly.
quests.pacingRule: Accelerated Pacing: Chaos in narration is quick.

quests.word: And it was in that moment that I understood what he'd been trying to tell me all along.
quests.textToSpeak: And it was in that moment that I understood what he'd been trying to tell me all along.
options: Decelerating (the moment of understanding is given time)
Accelerating (the narrator speeds up to get to the conclusion)
quests.correctAnswer: Decelerating (the moment of understanding is given time)
quests.hint: Is the speaker reporting an action, or revealing an insight?
quests.explanation: Realisations are best told with a slightly slower pace. It gives the listener time to share it.
quests.pacingRule: Decelerated Pacing: Moments of realisation are slowed.

quests.word: I didn't say the project failed, I said it wasn't finished.
quests.textToSpeak: I didn't say the project failed, I said it wasn't finished.
options: Decelerating (the contrast between the two claims is delivered clearly)
Accelerating (the speaker moves briskly to avoid a fuss)
quests.correctAnswer: Decelerating (the contrast between the two claims is delivered clearly)
quests.hint: What is the difference between 'failed' and 'wasn't finished'?
quests.explanation: The whole sentence is a correction. If 'failed' and 'wasn't finished' run together, the correction disappears.
quests.pacingRule: Decelerated Pacing: Corrections and contrasts are slowed.

quests.word: It's not a big deal, it's a tiny fix, it'll take two minutes.
quests.textToSpeak: It's not a big deal, it's a tiny fix, it'll take two minutes.
options: Decelerating (the speaker slows to show how careful the fix is)
Accelerating (minimising the problem is done with light speed)
quests.correctAnswer: Accelerating (minimising the problem is done with light speed)
quests.hint: What is the speaker trying to get the listener to feel?
quests.explanation: The listener should feel it's small. A quick, dismissive pace creates that impression.
quests.pacingRule: Accelerated Pacing: Minimising is quick.

quests.word: We have plenty of ideas, but what we lack is time.
quests.textToSpeak: We have plenty of ideas, but what we lack is time.
options: Decelerating (the word 'lack' and the contrast are given emphasis)
Accelerating (the speaker hurries since the point is obvious)
quests.correctAnswer: Decelerating (the word 'lack' and the contrast are given emphasis)
quests.hint: Which half of the sentence is the problem?
quests.explanation: The second half, 'what we lack is time', is the real problem and the first half only sets it up. Slowing there lets the contrast land.
quests.pacingRule: Decelerated Pacing: The problem half of a contrast is slowed.

quests.word: So I went to the shop, it was closed, I went to the next one, it was closed, and by then I was furious.
quests.textToSpeak: So I went to the shop, it was closed, I went to the next one, it was closed, and by then I was furious.
options: Accelerating (the repeating pattern goes quickly to show the frustration)
Decelerating (the speaker slows on each closed shop for comedy)
quests.correctAnswer: Accelerating (the repeating pattern goes quickly to show the frustration)
quests.hint: What is the joke or point of this story?
quests.explanation: The repetition shows the pattern. Speed shows that it got worse quickly and that the speaker lost patience.
quests.pacingRule: Accelerated Pacing: Repetitive patterns in a story are quick.

quests.word: I waited, and I waited, and eventually, just when I'd given up, the door opened.
quests.textToSpeak: I waited, and I waited, and eventually, just when I'd given up, the door opened.
options: Accelerating (the narrator hurries so that the story does not drag)
Decelerating (the stretch of waiting is conveyed by slowing the telling)
quests.correctAnswer: Decelerating (the stretch of waiting is conveyed by slowing the telling)
quests.hint: What is the narrator describing, and how long did it feel?
quests.explanation: Time stretching out is shown in the pace. The slow part makes the ending surprising.
quests.pacingRule: Decelerated Pacing: Waiting in a story is told slowly.

quests.word: The next morning was a blur of packing, phone calls, and lukewarm coffee.
quests.textToSpeak: The next morning was a blur of packing, phone calls, and lukewarm coffee.
options: Decelerating (the list is slowed so the listener can picture each thing)
Accelerating (a blur is narrated with speed to suit it)
quests.correctAnswer: Accelerating (a blur is narrated with speed to suit it)
quests.hint: What does the word 'blur' say about the pace of the morning?
quests.explanation: A 'blur' is fast and indistinct, and the narration imitates it. A slow list would make each task sound separate and clear.
quests.pacingRule: Accelerated Pacing: Blurs are narrated quickly.

quests.word: Here's what most people don't realise: the cheapest option often costs the most over time.
quests.textToSpeak: Here's what most people don't realise: the cheapest option often costs the most over time.
options: Accelerating (the claim is delivered quickly as a witty line)
Decelerating (a counter-intuitive claim is given space to be absorbed)
quests.correctAnswer: Decelerating (a counter-intuitive claim is given space to be absorbed)
quests.hint: What does the audience believe before the speaker says this?
quests.explanation: They believe cheap is best. Their belief must be replaced, which takes time.
quests.pacingRule: Decelerated Pacing: Counter-intuitive claims are slowed.

quests.word: Now, I won't bore you with the methodology, it's all in the appendix.
quests.textToSpeak: Now, I won't bore you with the methodology, it's all in the appendix.
options: Decelerating (the speaker slows to assure the audience that it's available)
Accelerating (a disclaimer that skips details is delivered quickly)
quests.correctAnswer: Accelerating (a disclaimer that skips details is delivered quickly)
quests.hint: What is the speaker choosing to do with the content they mention?
quests.explanation: The speaker is skipping it. Brisk delivery is the audio version of skipping.
quests.pacingRule: Accelerated Pacing: Skipped content is brisk.

quests.word: So, to bring it all together, the evidence points in one direction, and it's the one we least expected.
quests.textToSpeak: So, to bring it all together, the evidence points in one direction, and it's the one we least expected.
options: Accelerating (the conclusion is fast because the audience already knows it)
Decelerating (the conclusion and its surprise are delivered with deliberate pacing)
quests.correctAnswer: Decelerating (the conclusion and its surprise are delivered with deliberate pacing)
quests.hint: Where is the audience expecting to hear the answer?
quests.explanation: The whole talk has led to this. A conclusion given in a hurry seems unimportant.
quests.pacingRule: Decelerated Pacing: Conclusions are slowed.
